text.p: Here are the highlights from Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Estonian and Russian foreign ministers met in the Russian city of Petroskoi on Tuesday and aprroved a draft agreement on their border.
- A trade agreement with Russia has been prepared and is expected to be approved now the border issue seems to have been resolved.
- The parliament approved a decree to construct three major cultural institutions - a national music academy, a national art museum and a national museum.
- A petition with 4,500 signatures has been presented to the government urging it not to cut student public transport subsidies.
- Estonian Air and SAS are negotiating an agreement to share the Tallinn-Copenhagen route. SAS wants to maintain its two flights per week but Estonia Air insists that it reduce the number to one.
